messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach for route /v1/generate (model=text-gen-v2, region=us-west1). Current p95=250ms, p99=2.6s, error-rate spike 1.8%. Streaming sessions showing stalls (~5-10s stall windows). Affected customers: acme-corp (high), beta-infra (medium). Auto-scale attempted. Paging on-call (policy: sev-2).

jade_oncall: acked. I'm on it, pulling metrics and recent deploys.

mike_sre: joining. seeing tail spike aligning with thermal events on node gpu-node-43. nvml shows GPU utilisation steady but PCIe errors incrementing.

sam_ml: I'm on models. No new model deploys in last 6h. Traffic pattern unchanged. Could be infra.

nina_support: acme-corp reporting degraded streaming experience in prod chat widgets. Their logs show repeated reconnects. Customer impact: messages delayed, a few timeouts. CC: amanda_acme_support.

jade_oncall: timeline: p99 started climbing ~2002101040, hit 2.6s at 2002101105. Correlated with node GPU temp rising. I'm grabbing node logs.

mike_sre: paste from dmesg on gpu-node-43:

```
[Aug 12 09:15:42] NVRM: GPU 0000:06:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:06:00): 79, PID=2143 0x00000040 0x00000000
[Aug 12 09:15:42] kernel: pcieport 0000:02:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[Aug 12 09:16:01] NVRM: GPU 0000:06:00.0: RmAccessProcessor: Attempted to access from freed process
[Aug 12 09:16:47] nvml: ECC errors detected on GPU 0: l1 cache single-bit
[Aug 12 09:17:12] thermal 0000:06:00.0: sensor temp=92C
```

mike_sre: nvml shows ECC single-bit corrected errors incrementing rapidly. Kernel logs show PCIe AER events and a couple of GPU resets. Temps are high (90-93C). That suggests thermal throttling + ephemeral ECC spikes.

sam_ml: thermal throttling would explain KV cache stalls and streaming stalls (streams waiting on GPU kernel). If kernel resets occur, that can break long-lived streaming connections and inflate tail latencies.

jade_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) drain gpu-node-43 and live-migrate pods; 2) route new streaming sessions away from us-west1 to us-west2 temporarily; 3) enable CPU-fallback for streaming sessions for high-priority customers; 4) scale up cold pool of smaller GPUs to absorb traffic. Thoughts?

mike_sre: start with drain + traffic reroute. I'll kick off drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then cordon. Also add node to maintenance pool in autoscaler.

jade_oncall: noted. I'll add routing rule in the router: increase weight to us-west2 for /v1/generate for 50% of traffic, and set canary fallback for acme-corp -> 100% us-west2.

ops-bot: Autoscaler: added 4 n1-standard-8 + small-gpu instances in us-west2, estimated warmup 120s.

mike_sre: drain started at 2002101158. Log: `Evicting pod text-gen-001..` Some pods took >30s to terminate due to KV cache flush. Streaming sessions: ~18 active; we gracefully drained 12, 6 were force-terminated.

sam_ml: forcing some long-lived streams caused a small increase in 5xxs for a minute, but overall throughput recovered as sessions reconnected to us-west2.

nina_support: updated acme status: informing them of mitigation steps and that we're failing over to another region. They've asked for ETA on full recovery.

jade_oncall: current metrics post-reroute: p95=210ms, p99=420ms. Streaming stall rate down from 3.2% -> 0.6%. Error-rate back to baseline. Customer reconnections still trickling.

mike_sre: hardware-team pinged. We should collect ECC counters and a full nvflash out-of-band for analysis. If ECC persists after reboot, request RMA.

hardware-team: acknowledged. Please preserve machine for debug. We'll want `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` output and power/thermal telemetry.

jade_oncall: I'm scheduling a rolling reboot of gpu-node-43 after we finish evacuations. Planning: reboot window at 2002101230. Will coordinate with hardware-team.

mike_sre: note: one of the rack PDUs reported minor voltage sag earlier (ops alert at 2002101035), could explain thermal/power instability causing ECC noise. Ops to confirm.

ops-bot: PDU monitoring: rack-r12 reported transient voltage drop - 4 events between 2002101000-2002101045, amplitude -6% for ~6s each. Logged.

hardware-team: if PDUs show sags, please isolate the node and power-cycle the PDU outlet. We'll also run memtest on the host and check ECC counts after a cold boot.

jade_oncall: doing a controlled power-cycle of the node's outlet now (ops runbook step).

mike_sre: after power-cycle and reboot, ECC counters reset to nominal and no new corrected errors for 12 minutes of observation. Temps stabilized at 68-72C under similar load.

sam_ml: model-side checks: no evidence of degradation in logits or hallucination rate. QoS looks fine.

nina_support: acme-corp update: they see chat responsiveness normalizing, they've accepted the workaround and asked for postmortem.

jade_oncall: immediate incident wrap: traffic reroute + node drain + PDU power-cycle + node reboot returned latency to acceptable levels. We'll keep node cordoned until hardware-team completes tests.

mike_sre: follow-ups: 1) run full hardware diagnostics and memtest on gpu-node-43; 2) investigate PDU events and rack power distribution; 3) consider replacing PDU or moving critical nodes to different circuits; 4) add extra NVML ECC counter alert at lower threshold to catch early spikes; 5) add streaming session graceful handoff improvements to reduce forced-termination 5xxs.

hardware-team: agree. We'll schedule onsite check and RMA if ECC reappears. We'll also inspect cabling and PSU health.

jade_oncall: postmortem owner: mike_sre. I'll draft immediate incident note for customers and coordinate timeline.

mike_sre: assigning postmortem action items and will follow up in a separate thread. Closing this thread for live coordination. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2002101322 by jade_oncall. Severity downgraded to P3 for hardware follow-up.
